title: California upwelling winds did not continue their 1982-2008 rise in 2009-2025 (buoys, CUTI); Oregon-Washington upwelling rose; inland heat did not predict the change
abstract: Question: did upwelling-favourable alongshore wind in the California Current System (31-48 N, April-July) continue the increase that was reported for 1982-2008, and does inland heating (the Bakun mechanism) explain the change? Data: measured wind stress at 23 NDBC buoys (888 station-years, 1975-2025), the CUTI and BEUTI transport indices (1988-2025), the PFEL Bakun sea-level-pressure index (1967-2025) and CPC daily land Tmax. Method: trends with block-bootstrap intervals; an out-of-sample test that fits a line on 1982-2008 and predicts 2009-2025; latitude regression; daily lag and interannual regressions of stress on inland Tmax. The plan was written before the results. Results: at central California buoys (35.8-38.2 N) the 1982-2008 slopes were +8 to +16% per decade, but 2009-2025 means were 14-33% below the extrapolated trend. For CUTI 35-42 N the extrapolation predicted 2009-2025 worse than no change (skill -1.94, 95% interval -9.6 to -0.28); for 9 pooled California buoys skill was -0.31 (-6.4 to 0.44). The 2009-2025 forcing was only +0.22 to +0.28 SD above 1982-2008 (not clear). Off Oregon-Washington, CUTI 44-47 N rose by +0.92 SD (p 0.005) and the trend continued (skill +0.53), in the direction of projected poleward intensification. Inland Tmax warmed by +0.70 SD, but the interannual sensitivity of California buoy stress to inland Tmax was near zero (-2.5 to +4.4% per K, none clear); daily wind anomalies led inland heat, not the reverse. The Bakun index showed a larger rise (+22% per decade at 39 N) that drifted from the buoy record by 0.36-0.57 SD per decade at 4 of 5 buoys, so we do not use it as evidence of intensification. Limitations: buoy anemometer-height changes are not corrected; the test period has 17 seasons and most single-series intervals are wide; CUTI changes product in 2011 (no clear step found); climate modes were not modelled.

display.caption: April-July upwelling forcing anomalies (SD) for California buoys and CUTI 35-42 N, the Bakun index, and Oregon-Washington. Dashed lines: 1982-2008 linear fit extended to 2025. Thick bars: period means. The California increase did not continue after 2008; the Oregon-Washington increase continued.

Left: April-July trend by latitude (% of the 1991-2020 mean per decade, 95% block-bootstrap intervals) for coastal buoys, CUTI and the Bakun index. Right: 1982-2008 slope (circles) and the 2009-2025 mean minus the extrapolated trend (squares).

Left: correlation of daily April-July anomalies of buoy alongshore stress and inland Tmax at lags -2 to +3 days (positive lag: Tmax leads). Right: observed 1982-2025 buoy stress trend versus the trend predicted from inland warming and the interannual sensitivity.

citations.reason: Bakun (1990) hypothesis of upwelling intensification from land-sea contrast; we test its mechanism and trend.
Garcia-Reyes and Largier (2010) reported increased upwelling winds at central California buoys in 1982-2008; we find a similar early slope that did not continue in 2009-2025.
Jacox et al. (2018) CUTI and BEUTI indices.
Rykaczewski et al. (2015) projected poleward intensification; Oregon-Washington CUTI agrees in direction.
Sydeman et al. (2014) meta-analysis of upwelling intensification.
Bograd et al. (2009) spring transition definition.
PFEL Bakun upwelling index (erdUI306hr to erdUI486hr).
